newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares virtually unchanged, correction looms.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares virtually unchanged, correction looms.

text.p: Danish share prices closed a smidgen higher on Wednesday after falling from early heights, with dealers seeing correction ahead in a market focused on Wall Street but suffering from a dearth of buyers.
"We rose initially on FOMC's decision to leave U.S. rates untouched but fell back later. We could well see correction now after the recent weeks' rises," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index closed only 0.03 point up at 167.53 after hitting a high 168.10 earlier in the day. The KFX June future rose 0.95 point to 168.15 with 291 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Interest focused again on A.P. Moeller paper, with D/S 1912 closing 2,500 higher at 245,000 and twin D/S Svendborg 1,000 crowns up at 350,000.
Danisco was also very much in the limelight, climbing to 398 only to sink back along with the rest of the market, ending the day two crowns lower at 393.
Overall turnover for the day was 1.134 billion crowns.
